steps.say: A quadrilateral has 4 sides. Here are six kinds.

figure.alt: A square, a rectangle, a rhombus, a parallelogram, a trapezium and a kite.

steps.say: Parallel sides go in the same direction and never meet. A parallelogram has 2 pairs.

figure.alt: A parallelogram leaning to the right.

steps.say: A trapezium has exactly 1 pair of parallel sides.

figure.alt: A trapezium with a long bottom side and a shorter top side.

steps.say: A kite has two pairs of equal sides next to each other. It has 1 line of symmetry.

figure.alt: A kite with its vertical line of symmetry.

steps.say: A regular polygon has all sides equal and all angles equal.

check.prompt: Which quadrilateral has exactly one pair of parallel sides?

options.why: A parallelogram has two pairs of parallel sides.
A rectangle has two pairs of parallel sides.
A kite has no parallel sides.

hints: Parallel sides never meet, however long they get.
Look at the opposite sides of each shape.
Count the pairs for each shape.
check.explanation: A trapezium has exactly one pair of parallel sides.

check.prompt: How many lines of symmetry does a square have?
hints: A line of symmetry splits a shape into two matching halves.
Try lines up and down, and across.
Try the lines from corner to corner too.
check.explanation: A square has 2 lines through the middles of its sides and 2 lines from corner to corner. That makes 4.
